source.name: fn_FormatCustomerName

assumptions: NVARCHAR(100) mapped to VARCHAR(100) - PostgreSQL VARCHAR is Unicode-capable by default
NVARCHAR(201) mapped to VARCHAR(201) for return type
Function marked as IMMUTABLE since it has no side effects and returns consistent results for the same inputs
ISNULL() converted to COALESCE() - functionally equivalent in this context
String concatenation operator '+' converted to '||' (PostgreSQL standard)
Parameter names prefixed with 'p_' to follow PostgreSQL naming conventions and avoid reserved word conflicts
Schema 'dbo' preserved - ensure this schema exists in PostgreSQL or adjust as needed

reviewFlags.reason: Verify that VARCHAR(201) provides sufficient length for all expected customer name combinations. PostgreSQL VARCHAR has no performance penalty for larger declarations, so consider using TEXT or a larger limit if needed.

Confirm that VARCHAR encoding matches application expectations. PostgreSQL uses database encoding (typically UTF-8) for all text types, which may handle multi-byte characters differently than SQL Server NVARCHAR.

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server NVARCHAR uses UTF-16 encoding while PostgreSQL VARCHAR uses the database encoding (typically UTF-8). Character length limits may behave differently with multi-byte characters.
Function marked as IMMUTABLE for optimal query optimization. This assumes the function will always return the same result for the same inputs, which is true for this string formatting function.
COALESCE() in PostgreSQL behaves identically to ISNULL() in SQL Server for this two-argument case, returning the first non-NULL value.
